region.text: Fort Nassau 'up Hudson's River' in the Albany area

ledger.note: 1614: the Dutch plant Fort Nassau on the Hudson. 'It is likely that Hudson's peaceful contact with the Mohicans encouraged them to establish Fort Nassau in 1614'; 'The States General issued patents in 1614 for the development of New Netherland as a private, commercial venture.'

region.text: Fort Orange and Noten Eylant

ledger.note: 1624: the first families land. 'in May 1624, the GWC landed 30 families at Fort Orange' and Noten Eylant (Governors Island); 'In 1624, New Netherland became a province of the Dutch Republic.'
1626: New Amsterdam on Manhattan becomes the colony's seat; the infobox names New Amsterdam as the capital but the page does not date the move from Fort Orange.

region.text: the Connecticut River settlements, Fort Goede Hoop on the 'Fresh River'

ledger.note: 1626: Connecticut cells appear in Cliopatria's shape. The page mentions 'a few Dutch settlers ... at Fort Goede Hoop on the Fresh River' without a date; the year is Cliopatria's (page silent). [Reviewer am-06-c, 2026-10-19: region narrowed from the whole of Connecticut and Massachusetts (129 cells) to the Connecticut cells of the Cliopatria 1626 shape (16 cells) that keyframe 2 draws.]

region.text: the island of Manhattan, bought for the West India Company

ledger.note: 1626: Minuit acquires Manhattan. 'Peter Minuit and Walloon colonists of the West India Company acquired the island of Manhattan on 24 May 1626.' New Amsterdam becomes the seat (infobox capital).

region.text: the extra New Jersey, Delaware valley and Hudson cells of the 1632 shape

ledger.note: 1632: the shape grows by about a dozen cells, mostly in New Jersey (Fort Nassau on the Delaware, which the page mentions only as dismantled in 1651). The page is silent on the year.

region.text: the extra Connecticut River and Hudson cells of the 1636 shape

ledger.note: 1636: nine more New York and 14 more Connecticut cells appear, and two in Massachusetts. The page is silent on the year.

region.text: the Connecticut River region: 'Stuyvesant provisionally ceded the Connecticut River region to New England'

ledger.note: 1650 (19 September): the Treaty of Hartford. 'The treaty was signed on September 19' between Stuyvesant and Governor Edward Hopkins of Connecticut; the Dutch gave up claims 'the full length of the Connecticut River ... east to Narragansett Bay' for a Long Island line from Oyster Bay. The Dutch West India Company approved it; the English government did not. [Reviewer am-06-c, 2026-10-19: region narrowed to the Connecticut-valley cells of the Cliopatria 1648 shape (26 cells), the land keyframe 10 removes; the Treaty of Hartford page names the Connecticut River claim and does not mention Massachusetts.]

region.text: Fort Casimir on the west bank of the Delaware

ledger.note: 1651: Fort Casimir. 'In 1651, the Dutch dismantled Fort Nassau and constructed Fort Casimir on the west bank.' Built opposite the Swedish settlements; the page does not say who held the ground before.

region.text: Fort Casimir

ledger.note: 1654 (May): New Sweden strikes. 'In May 1654, soldiers from New Sweden led by Governor Johan Risingh captured Fort Casimir and renamed it Fort Trinity.' In November 1654 the Company ordered Stuyvesant to drive the Swedes from the river.

region.text: Fort Casimir, renamed Fort Trinity

ledger.note: 1654 (May): Fort Casimir falls to the Swedes under Johan Risingh.

region.text: Fort Casimir (Fort Trinity), retaken by Stuyvesant

ledger.note: 1655: Stuyvesant retakes the fort. He 'quickly retook Fort Casimir (Fort Trinity)' after sailing from New Amsterdam with 7 ships and 317 soldiers; the page gives no day.

region.text: New Sweden on the Delaware: Fort Christina and the settlements 'on both sides of the Delaware River'

ledger.note: 1655 (15 September): New Sweden falls. 'Stuyvesant then proceeded to besiege Fort Christina which surrendered on September 15, 1655'; 'New Sweden was conquered by the Dutch Republic in 1655 and incorporated into the Dutch colony of New Netherland.' The Swedes kept their militia, religion and court. Cliopatria ends New Sweden in 1658.

region.text: the lower Delaware

ledger.note: 1655 (15 September): the Delaware fighting ends with the surrender of Fort Christina.

region.text: New Amsterdam's harbour on Gravesend Bay, Long Island

ledger.note: 1664 (27 August): the English fleet arrives. 'They arrived at Gravesend Bay on Long Island on August 27' under Richard Nicolls; the Navy's 'four English frigates ... demanded New Netherland's surrender' (New Netherland page); Charles II had granted the land between the Delaware and the Connecticut to the Duke of York in March.

region.text: New Amsterdam and Long Island

ledger.note: 1664 (8 September): New Amsterdam surrenders. 'The Articles were signed September 6, and the transfer took place September 8'; Dutch colonists kept their property, laws and religion.

region.text: Fort Orange, renamed Fort Albany

ledger.note: 1664 (24 September): Fort Orange surrenders. 'on September 24, 1664 vice-director of New Netherland Johannes de Montagne surrendered the fort to the English'; renamed Fort Albany the next day. Esopus 'surrendered without resistance' (undated).

region.text: New Netherland

ledger.note: 1664 (September): the conquest is complete. 'The Peace of Breda that ended the Second Anglo-Dutch War left New York in English hands.'

region.text: the Delaware: Fort Casimir (New Amstel) and the settlements on the lower river

ledger.note: 1664 (September, undated): the Delaware. Sir Robert Carr's campaign took Fort Casimir by storm ('fired two broadsides into the fort') 'around the same time' as Fort Orange; New Amstel was renamed New Castle. [Reviewer am-06-c, 2026-10-19: month 9 -> 10 and source -> New Sweden page, which says the English conquest of 1664 ended with the capture of Fort Casimir (New Amstel) in October; the Conquest page gives no date for it.]

region.text: Staten Island and New York harbour

ledger.note: 1673 (28 July, Old Style): the Dutch fleet reaches Staten Island with '21 ships (including prizes)'.

region.text: New Netherland 're-established as a Dutch colony', of which the page documents the town of New York ('New Orange') and Fort James

ledger.note: 1673 (9 August, New Style): the Dutch retake New York. The fleet fired on the fort, Anthony Colve's troops landed and Captain Manning 'was granted the honors of war'; 'New Netherland was re-established as a Dutch colony'. The extent beyond New York is the researcher's reading (the page names no outlying settlement).

region.text: New York

ledger.note: 1673 (9 August): the fort surrenders; New York is re-christened New Orange.

region.text: New Netherland, which the Dutch 'gave up ... in exchange for Suriname' under the Treaty of Westminster

ledger.note: 1674 (10 November, New Style): the handover. 'In February 1674, the Treaty of Westminster concluded the war' and the transfer 'eventually took place on 10 November 1674' when Edmund Andros replaced Colve. The Dutch kept Suriname and Run (Treaty of Breda, 1667, New Netherland page).

region.text: New Netherland

ledger.note: 1674: New Netherland ends for good after sixty years. The Dutch keep Suriname.

wars.name: Dutch conquest of New Sweden

zones.text: the lower Delaware, Fort Casimir and Fort Christina

wars.outcome: Dutch victory: Fort Casimir taken by the Swedes in May 1654, retaken by Stuyvesant in 1655, Fort Christina surrendered on 15 September 1655.
wars.note: Stuyvesant sailed from New Amsterdam with 7 ships and 317 soldiers.

wars.name: English conquest of New Netherland

zones.text: New Amsterdam, Fort Orange and the Delaware

wars.outcome: English victory: New Amsterdam surrendered on 8 September 1664, Fort Orange on 24 September; the Peace of Breda that ended the Second Anglo-Dutch War 'left New York in English hands'.
wars.note: The Wikipedia articles are 'Conquest of New Netherland' and 'Second Anglo-Dutch War'; the 1667 end year is the war's, not on the page.

wars.name: Reconquest of New Netherland

zones.text: New York (New Orange) and the colony of New Netherland

wars.outcome: Dutch recapture on 9 August 1673; the Treaty of Westminster (February 1674) gave New Netherland back to England in exchange for Suriname, and the handover took place on 10 November 1674.
wars.note: Part of the Third Anglo-Dutch War; the page documents only New York town and the fort.

certainty.note: Trading posts and a claim 'from the Delmarva Peninsula to Cape Cod' with the Susquehanna as the Virginia boundary: no surveyed frontier.

The Hartford line of 19 September 1650 (Connecticut border and Oyster Bay on Long Island) is sharp, 'with minor adjustments' today's Connecticut-New York border; every other frontier is soft. 1665-1672 is the English interval (no Dutch land).

notes: Cliopatria's 'New Netherland' row (1622..1802) is not one state: its shapes bundle New Netherland proper (the Hudson valley, Long Island, Connecticut River, New Jersey and the Delaware, 1622-1669) with the Dutch West India Company's other colonies. By gazetteer overlap of the shapes: Essequibo/Guyana cells from 1622, Saint Martin from 1629, Pernambuco and then all north-east Brazil (967 cells in 1642-44, 344,000 km2) from 1632 to 1653, Curacao and Aruba from 1636, Suriname from 1670 and Guyana until 1796, Saint Martin alone in 1800-02. This dossier keeps New Netherland proper and marks the rest (verdict adjust or, from 1670, wrong). Those colonies are written as separate dossiers by this batch: dutch-brazil (New Holland, 1630-1654), essequibo (with Demerara), berbice and dutch-suriname (Dutch Guiana, 1667-1975, which Cliopatria also lumps under Netherlands Antilles 1820-2023); none is in polities.csv. Dutch Curacao, Aruba and Saint Martin are still without dossiers (curacao, aruba, sint-maarten). Without them these lands vanish from the map. Cliopatria keeps New Netherland to 1669 (the English took it in 1664) and the Connecticut cells to 1669 (Hartford, 1650). Its New Sweden row ends 1658; the page ends New Sweden in 1655. New Castle has no gazetteer name: coordinate -75.55, 39.66 (Fort Casimir, a few km2) used. Pages budget (9): six opened (one a stub) and no page was spent on the lumped colonies. The Directors-General list was not opened, so no rulers. Kieft's and the Esopus wars, Fort Nassau on the Delaware and Fort Goede Hoop are undated on the pages opened.
